title: Half of what number of degrees makes a half turn?
description: The blank in half a turn equals half of something equal to one hundred and eighty degrees is filled with the full turn of three hundred and sixty degrees. Keeko's doubt, that a full turn is one hundred and eighty degrees, is broken by the spoke that only reaches the opposite side.
teaching_notes: One idea: half a turn is half of a full turn, so the full turn is double one hundred and eighty. Watch for children who give the half turn as the full turn.

source: The measure of half a circle is 1/2 of a full turn. So, the
video_script.why: The child finds the full turn from the half turn of one hundred and eighty degrees.
video_script.substitution: A spoke turning round its centre shows that half a turn lands on the opposite side and a full turn comes back to the start.
video_script.anchor: the book's paper semicircle with a blank in half a turn = 1/2 of ____ = 180°
video_script.wrong_answer: a full turn is one hundred and eighty degrees
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says a full turn is one hundred and eighty degrees. That only sends the spoke to the opposite side, so the bubble is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: The blank is three hundred and sixty degrees, because half of it is one hundred and eighty

final_answer.spoken: the blank is three hundred and sixty degrees, because half of it is one hundred and eighty

maths_rules: half a turn = 1/2 of a full turn = 180 degrees
the full turn is double the half turn: 180 + 180 = 360
a spoke turned 180 degrees lies on the opposite side; only 360 degrees brings it back
video_script.design: The semicircle and its blank stay on the board. The number three hundred and sixty is written only in the answer beat.

<bookmark mark='ask'/>Half a turn is one hundred and eighty degrees. Half of what number gives that?

<bookmark mark='write'/>Write one hundred and eighty at the bottom left of the semicircle.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko says a full turn is one hundred and eighty degrees.
<bookmark mark='half'/>But half of one hundred and eighty is only ninety, not one hundred and eighty.
<bookmark mark='side'/>A spoke turned one hundred and eighty degrees lies on the opposite side. Only a full turn brings it back to the start.
